 Shri Parag S.Chaturvedi - Advocate for appellant.

High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Shri A.S.Baghel - Government Advocate for respondent/Sta
Shro Saurabh Awasthi - Advocate for objector.
Heard on I.A.No.23324 of 2019 - an application for intervention.

This application is not
maintainable.
Hence, I.A.No.23324 of 2019 stands dismissed.
Heard on I.A. No.13454 of 2024 - an application for suspension of sentence.

2. This is the second application seeking for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of appellant - Rajit Ram Maurya who has been convicted under Section 420/34 and Section 409 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to R.I. for 5 years respectively and fine of Rs.4,00,000/-
respectively, with default stipulations as mentioned in the impugned judgment dated 27.06.2019 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Jabalpur in S.T.No.267 of 2018.
All the sentences to run concurrently.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that he is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
He has not committed any offence in any manner.
It is submitted that out of total conviction of 5 years, he has already undergone the entire conviction period.
He is in custody since 19.01.2018.
He is undergoing the sentence of one and half years further R.I. on two counts for the default on payment of fine which was Rs.4,00,000/- on two counts.
He has already undergone one and half years sentence in lieu of deposit of fine amount.
2 CRA-7707-2019 There is no likelihood of early hearing of the appeal in near future.
The appellant is ready to abide by all the terms and conditions that may be imposed by this Court while considering his application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

4. P er contra, learned Panel Lawyer for the State as well as the learned counsel for the objector has objection to the aforesaid but they could not dispute the fact that he has already undergone more Rajit Ram Morya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2516975/
1 than six and a half years of jail sentence.

sentences.text: 5. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court deems it appropriate to allow the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

6. Accordingly, I.A. No.13454 of 2024 is allowed and it is directed that the remaining jail sentence of the appellant shall remain under suspension subject to the verification of the fact that the amount of fine has been deposited and he be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 10.12.2024 and thereafter on such other subsequent dates as may be fixed in that behalf.

At this stage, counsel for the appellant submits that he may be granted three months' time to arrange the fine amount and he will deposit the same before the Trial Court in pursuance to Crime No.863/2017.
In view of the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellant, he is granted three months time to deposit the fine amount before the Trial Court.
